pr_title: EVP: Implement data-driven translation between known ctrl and OSSL_PARAMs
pr_body:
The idea is to make it as transparent as possible to call things like
EVP_PKEY_CTX_ctrl() with a provider backed EVP_PKEY_CTX, or things
like EVP_PKEY_get_bn_param() with a legacy EVP_PKEY.

All these sorts of calls demand that we translate between ctrl
commands and OSSL_PARAM keys, and treat the arguments appropriately.

This implementation has it being as data driven as possible, thereby
centralizing everything into one table of translation data, which
supports both directions.

Fixes #13528
pr_comments: Note that this isn't finished yet, there are fixup functions missing.  However, the functionality and structure have crystallised enough to make the idea reviewable.  Please comment, even it doesn't build, early feedback welcome!
The fixup functions need to know the insize and outsize of all params, right? This means that third-party providers cant add new controls.  Or am I just misreading the code?

@richsalz, I think you've misunderstood the purpose.

1. This is entirely in libcrypto and about stuff *that libcrypto knows*.  Period.  Providers are not involved (more than being recipients of OSSL_PARAM data), at all.
2. This is a tool that translates between ctrl functions and ctrl command numbers *that libcrypto knows* and OSSL_PARAM functions and names *that libcrypto knows*, in both directions.

Regarding insize and outsize, the OSSL_PARAM structure already delivers that.  However, the limiting factor is the ctrl functions, which do not easily supply this (well, you can pass the insize as `p1`, and you can ask for an outsize with a *separate* ctrl command and passing the pointer to a `size_t` as `p2`...)

So in the end, this is meant to support calling `EVP_PKEY_CTX_ctrl()` with an `EVP_PKEY_CTX` that's set up for a provider backed operation, to support calling `EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_params()` with an `EVP_PKEY_CTX` that's set up for a legacy operation (limited to things libcrypto knows about), and to support calling `EVP_PKEY_get_bn_param()` with a legacy `EVP_PKEY`.

The life time of this source file is the same as the lifetime of legacy EVP_PKEYs, I totally expect them to be *gone* when ENGINE support is gone (ENGINE support being the last tangible reason why we retain legacy style EVP_PKEYs).  That's also a reason to have all of this collected into one file.

(while I'm at it, I also mean to clean away the current hackery which is spread all over the source instead of being concentrated to one spot, and that includes huge amounts of code copying ...  you've heard me battle that tendency before :wink:)

This would be a great improvement! It would also allow to drop all the new convenience functions such as EVP_PKEY_get_group_name(). But on the other hand they could still be kept, just with very much simplified implementation.

The most indicative is that some helper functions take pointers that aren't immediately transferable to OSSL_PARAMs, for example all the cipher and md setters, which take an EVP_CIPHER or EVP_MD. Oh boy, do we have...  "diverse" ways for ctrl functions to work.

Most have a different ctrl cmd for getting data vs for setting data.  There are a few exceptions, though, that set numbers via *p1*, except when *p1* == -2, which makes the ctrl work as a getter instead, with the address of the value storage in *p2*.

Most ctrl functions return simple numeric numbers as their return value.  Some, though, take an address to an int via *p2* instead.  This is understandable when the returned value may be a negative number, which indicates an error when returned as the return value (RSA-PSS saltlen has legitimate negative numbers, for example), but there are other cases that does this same thing without having real reason to (the RSA padding mode is a positive number bigger than zero).

issue_context.title: Calling EVP_PKEY_get_bn_param() on a legacy key does not work
issue_context.body:
For example if you have a DH legacy key stored in an EVP_PKEY, Calling EVP_PKEY_get_bn_parms() to get the p,g etc params does not work.

Also see #13522.
comments: Same issue applies to other "params" calls, e.g. `EVP_PKEY_get_utf8_string_param()`

@levitte : This is the reason for some failing SSL tests for the "ec deprecation" PR also.

Do you have any suggestions on how to handle this..
We just have a legacy key here with no pkey_ctx or keymanager (i.e it has a ameth) so I am not sure how this will be able to do an export here.
I assume a big special case 'switch' table here is not what we really want to do?

My suggestion is to continue to make specialized functions for all cases where we expect EVP_PKEYs to have either a legacy or a provided key.  See #13436.

In the future, when legacy stuff is removed, we will have to deprecate them and turn to pure OSSL_PARAM support, but as long as we have legacy stuff, this is the path we're already on.

We may need to discuss this within OTC..
Since this pretty much makes the EVP_PKEY_get_XXXX_param() calls pretty much pointless.
(The getters assumed non-legacy use cases when they were written).

> Since this pretty much makes the EVP_PKEY_get_XXXX_param() calls pretty much pointless.

Er, no?

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/81aef6ba720971c09ad68f89d418c8d3d3f904f7/crypto/evp/p_lib.c#L1260-L1263

I hear you, though.  And yeah, it's perfectly possible to to the reverse of what we've done with ctrls, i.e. a params-to-legacy function to support the transition.

Are you willing to code that?

>  Er, no?

Having to check whether a key is legacy or not if quite horrific from an end user perspective (this should be an internal implementation detail that they are not aware of).

> Having to check whether a key is legacy or not if quite horrific from an end user perspective (this should be an internal implementation detail that they are not aware of).

I wasn't implying that they should have to do that.

So...  are we done discussing approaches?  I can accept that we will make the diverse EVP_PKEY_get_*_param functions work with legacy keys, and my proposal is params-to-legacy translation of all the things we're interested in.  That involves extracting the underlying type (RSA, DSA, ...) and extracting numbers from it in some cases, or calling a ctrl function in other cases.

Another approach, which I think has been mentioned, is to do the automated export to provider and make the appropriate get_params() call.  I see an issue with that one, though, that it cannot support ENGINE backed keys (not even those with open data, since they are unlikely to have implemented the required export function).

If we're done discussing, it might be time to code...

@levitte I may have some time to look at this. The params-to-legacy approach, extracting fields from the new API to return via legacy APIs, would be my first choice but I'd need to prototype something to see how feasible it is. Let me know if you have any more helpful insights!

I had an idea now that this calls for a bit of refactoring, to give translation data more of a two way flair.

I mean, the "easy" way is to create a separate set of functions that do the inverse of `legacy_ctrl_to_param` and friends, but that comes with a cost of one more spot to keep track of and potential loss of sync.

The idea in my mind is a set of small functions with a table of data that drives ctrl\<-\>params translation in one go.

So er, you or me?
@levitte Ah ok. I'm continuing to dig up and investigate other issues which may or may not be related, so I'm a long way from coding this. I'm happy to leave this one to you.
@levitte is the bottleneck currently - so probably not a good idea to assign to him.

Well...  I'm already well ahead, so I might as well finish it up.
(what I'm doing will also clean away huge amounts of code copying)

One thing we need to be aware of is that there's no way we can support EVP_PKEY_get_bn_param() on ENGINE-implemented key types that we know nothing about.  That translation capability is simply not there, and never was.  On the other hand, there has never been any support to extract payload from such keys, so it's probably not something to worry about.
